title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 250
text:
23. Section 2(1) sets out the definition of a person who lacks capacity:
“A person lacks capacity in relation to a matter if at the material time he is unable to make a
decision for himself in relation to the matter because of an impairment of, or a disturbance
in the functioning of, the mind or brain.”
Capacity is thus decision-specific, but it does not matter whether the impairment or
disturbance is permanent or temporary.

24. Section 3 provides that a person is unable to make a decision if unable to:
• Understand the information relevant to the decision.
• Retain that information.
• Use or weigh that information as part of the process of making the decision.
• Communicate their decision (whether by talking, using sign language or any other
means).

25. Explanations must be provided in ways that are appropriate to the person’s circumstances.
This can include explanations in simple language, use of visual aids etc.
